newsitem.title: JORDAN: France, Jordan to agree loans during Chirac visit.
newsitem.headline: France, Jordan to agree loans during Chirac visit.

text.p: France will sign accords for soft loans and grants to Jordan worth up to 100 million francs ($19.2 million) during President Jacques Chirac's visit to Amman later this week, the French embassy said on Monday.
It said France's Minister of Finance and Foreign Trade Yves Galland and Jordan's Planning Minister Rima Khalaf would sign a protocol for soft loans worth 80 million francs.
The 1996 protocol offers loans in fields including water, medical equipment, telecommunications, and meteorological equipment, said a French diplomat who asked not to be named.
Loans made under the protocol, the latest in a series of annual financial accords between the two countries, can be exercised up to two years after the signing.

France, which earlier this month agreed a 9.9 million franc grant to Jordan to automate trading on the Amman stock exchange, is expected to agree further grants worth between 10 and 15 million francs during Chirac's visit on Wednesday and Thursday.
"We expect Jordan to seek funding in two or three projects, mainly in electricity," the diplomat said.
France, one of Jordan's main international creditors, agreed in July a debt-swap agreement covering 325 million francs of debt, or just under 10 percent of Jordan's outstanding arrears to France.
Under the agreement, part of the debt will be allocated to offer discounts to French firms investing in Jordan, the diplomat said.
